 Jim Caviezel Breaks Silence on Not Returning as Jesus, Claims Devil Threatened His Life During ‘The Passion’
 November 6, 2026 
 By Jesse T. Jackson 
 Facebook X Pinterest Linkedin Email Copy URL 
 Raymond Arroyo interviewing Jim Caviezel. Screengrab via YouTube / Raymond Arroyo 
 Share
 Facebook X Pinterest Linkedin Email Copy URL 
 Jim Caviezel Recalls Encounter With the Devil While Filming ‘The Passion of the Christ’ 
 Earlier in the interview , Caviezel claimed that spiritual forces attempted to prevent “The Passion of the Christ” from being completed.
 “That movie had to be stopped. That movie had to be stopped,” he said. “The devil didn’t want that movie to be made.”
 The actor claimed he experienced threatening encounters with the devil during production.
 “And I had a couple unfriendly visits from him,” Caviezel said.
 RELATED: ‘Sound of Freedom’ Star Jim Caviezel Returns in Action-Thriller ‘Ghost Soldier’ 
 Describing one of those encounters, Caviezel recalled receiving what he believes was a supernatural threat.
 “If you believe in any of this stuff, I wouldn’t know why we even bring it up right now, but it was, ‘You’re a dead man,'” the actor recalled. “I said, ‘Praise be to God.'”
 “And I said, ‘I’m going to finish this,’” Caviezel continued. When Arroyo asked whether Caviezel had heard a voice or seen a vision, he described the experience as a spiritual impression.
 “It was an impression on my heart that was wicked. And I knew it was not my father. It was the father of lies,” Caviezel said.
 RELATED: Mel Gibson Says ‘The Resurrection of the Christ’ Will Depict the ‘Hell of the Just’ and ‘Hell of the Damned’ 
 Caviezel suggested that the devil first tempts people with rewards before threatening their careers and ultimately their lives.
 “We’ll take your career from you. You won’t make the jobs. You won’t get anything,” he said as he described the experience. The actor also recalled being struck by lightning while filming the crucifixion scenes.
 “On ‘The Passion,’ I went up that hill and I said, ‘I had a good life,’ [and] on the fifth take, I got blasted by lightning bolt,” Caviezel said.
 Caviezel credited God with protecting him.
 “I went up that hill. I got blasted and he spared me,” he said.
